design_philosophy: Strict Object-Oriented Graph Schema with Mandatory Global Fields, Explicit Composition, Namespaces, Migration, Global Definitions, Scripted UDFs, Advanced Querying, Execution-Oriented Model, and Data-Oriented Storage

syntax_rules.termination: All statements must be terminated by a semicolon (;).
syntax_rules.trailing_commas: Trailing commas are allowed in all list and struct contexts.

comments.termination_interaction: A comment is not a statement and does not require a semicolon.
valid_positions: Between entries in a batch [ ] block
Between fields in a type body { }
comments.lexer_interaction: Comments are consumed at the lexer stage and are invisible to the balanced-delimiter tokenizer. They do not contribute to any { } or [ ] nesting depth count.
comments.note: Line comments (//) are not supported. An unterminated /* produces [1001] Syntax Error.

unified_syntax_model.core_principle: HyperQL uses two bracket types with distinct, non-interchangeable semantics. { } is used for the contents of one thing (Body of a node, edge, function, object literal). [ ] is used for a batch of multiple siblings (Grouping multiple constructs of the same kind).

four_level_hierarchy.level_1: Singular construct. Terminated with ;. Example: DEFINE NODE Person { name, age };
four_level_hierarchy.level_2: Batch of same type. Multiple constructs under one keyword. Entries separated by ,. Example: DEFINE NODE [ Person { name, age }, Dog { name, breed } ];
four_level_hierarchy.level_3: Batch of multiple types. Multiple keywords grouped in an outer [ ]. Type keywords appear inside. Example: DEFINE [ FIELD [ name: String ], NODE [ Person { name } ] ];
four_level_hierarchy.level_4: Contained scope (NAMESPACE and SCHEMA). Introduces a named scope whose body is a [ ] batch.

storage_architecture.description: Global fields are logical constraints (interfaces), not physical storage locations. Data is physically partitioned by Node Type using a Data-Oriented Design (DOD) approach.

identity_model.schema_constructs: Every named schema construct (node, edge, field, role, etc.) is assigned a stable SchemaId (UUID v7) at definition time. It survives renames and is retired on DROP.
identity_model.data_instances: Every node and edge instance exposes a built-in virtual field `_id` (UUID v7, time-ordered), assigned at creation and immutable thereafter. Implicitly indexed as the primary partition lookup key.

implications: Queries specifying a type (MATCH (p:Person)) are optimized to scan only that type's partition.
Global queries (MATCH (n) WHERE n.LastName = 'X') require scanning all partitions containing that field.
To optimize global searches, use the CROSS_TYPE keyword or DEFINE MATERIALIZED VIEW.

tier_1_normative_semantics.description: All compliant implementations MUST satisfy these observable semantics.

requirements.spec: A query specifying a type must not read partitions for unrelated types
Null checks must not access field storage for null-valued rows
Variable-width fields must not be accessed for rows eliminated by earlier predicates
An available index that reduces scan scope must be used when its predicate matches
Must be equivalent to a stored property access — O(1)
All node and edge instances MUST provide a queryable `_id` field.
A non-nullable Node<T> field must always reference a valid _id of type T; child deletion is blocked by referential integrity.

tier_2_reference_guidance.description: Reference implementation details; normative ONLY for the HyperQL reference implementation. Other backends may differ.
details: Column-oriented contiguous arrays for fixed-width fields
Open-addressing hash sets for @unordered MANY roles
Sorted (node_id, edge_id) pairs in role index tables
UUID v7 for SchemaId and instance `_id`

0.1_hybrid_model.fixed_width_fields: Int, Int32, Float, Bool, Date, UUID, Decimal, Enum, Flags, Vector are stored column-oriented in contiguous arrays.
0.1_hybrid_model.variable_width_fields: String, List<T> are stored in a variable-length heap. Column store holds offset/length pairs. Filtering avoids heap access; projection accesses it only for rows surviving filters (Late Materialization).

normative_spec.0.2_struct_inline_guarantee: Struct fields are stored physically inline within the containing node's column store. No heap allocation or pointer indirection occurs for Struct access, providing maximum data locality.
normative_spec.0.2b_node_reference_storage: Node<T> fields store only the UUID v7 _id of the child node. The child node resides in its own type-specific partition. Accessing fields of a Node<T> child requires a partition lookup (dereference).
normative_spec.0.3_null_bitmap: Each partition maintains a null bitmap (one bit per nullable field per row). Null-checking (IS NULL, etc.) consults only the bitmap, never accessing field storage for null rows.

0.4_many_role_storage.@ordered: Dynamic array (O(n) scan, O(1) position access)
0.4_many_role_storage.@unordered: Open-addressing hash set (O(1) average membership test)

normative_spec.0.5_edge_storage: Dual-storage approach: Edge Partition stores edge fields column-oriented. Role Index Tables (one per role per edge type) store sorted (node_id, edge_id) pairs for O(log n) traversal.
normative_spec.0.6_vector_simd_alignment: Vector<N> fields must be 16/32-byte aligned and use Struct-of-Arrays layout for SIMD-accelerated similarity operations.
normative_spec.0.8_materialized_preference: @computed(TRAVERSE) @materialized is strongly preferred for production. It moves cost from read-time (graph scatter) to write-time (O(1) column lookup).
normative_spec.0.9_materialized_view: Creates dedicated cross-type partitions indexed by specified fields to optimize CROSS_TYPE queries from O(partitions * rows) to O(log n).
normative_spec.0.10_trigger_derivation: Triggers for @materialized fields are derived statically from the QueryPlan. Write operations (CREATE, SET, DELETE) on referenced edge types trigger atomic recomputation of affected nodes.

hoisting_and_validation.guarantee: All names are collected before references are resolved. Definition order does not affect validity.
passes: Pass 1 — Collection: Register all names (ENUM, FIELD, STRUCT, TRAIT, VIEW, UNION, NODE, EDGE, FUNCTION, INDEX)

Pass 2 — Type checking: Resolve all type references. v0.19 verifies matching DEFINE FIELD exists for all body references and rejects inline types [1052]. For multi-parent inheritance, checks for conflicting `display:` SchemaIds and raises [1057] if unresolved. Includes Node<T> reference resolution and validation of referenced types, view body type-checking, parameter inference, union variant field resolution, and return type checking for UDFs.
Pass 3 — Constraints: Validate expressions against resolved types, including cross-node constraints referencing Node<T> child fields.
Pass 4 — Edges: Validate inline role ALLOWS type references and constraint expressions in DEFINE EDGE
Pass 5 — Indexes: Validate DEFINE INDEX targets

inheritance_model.name: Composable Polymorphism
inheritance_model.description: EXTENDS implements field composition via global field definitions. Nodes and Edges may extend Traits and other concrete or abstract types. Multiple inheritance cannot create conflicts because all fields reference global DEFINE FIELD declarations. Traits are the abstraction mechanism. They are never instantiated but are queryable, participate in role ALLOWS resolution, and carry inheritable named constraints. Node<T> is the identity composition mechanism, allowing any node to contain a reference to another. Structs are the value composition mechanism. They carry no identity, participate in no graph relationships, and guarantee inline storage. The diamond problem is resolved by design — no conflicts are possible when all fields reference the same global definition.
inheritance_model.decorator_semantics: Decorators are properties of global field definitions, not inheritance paths. A field inherited from multiple parents retains decorators from its global definition.
inheritance_model.diamond_problem: Resolved by design - no conflicts possible when all fields reference the same global definition.

terminology.property: Instance-level data value (used interchangeably with field in queries)
terminology.hyperedge: Edge connecting multiple nodes via roles (HyperQL's primary edge model)
terminology.role: Named position in a hyperedge connecting to nodes, defined locally within the edge

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] NAMESPACE Name.Space [ ... ]; | DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] NAMESPACE Name.Space;
definitions.description: Declares the namespace for the current schema. Supports dot-hierarchy naming (Core.Game.Combat). Block form introduces a named scope whose body is a [ ] batch. All files contribute to their namespace under uniform validation rules. Inline field declarations are forbidden universally [1052].

preamble_form.description: Declares the file as a contributor to a namespace.
preamble_form.example:
DEFINE NAMESPACE Core.Game;
DEFINE FIELD level: Int;

block_form.description: Declares a self-contained namespace unit. Body is a [ ] batch. Standalone form uses full DEFINE keyword; contained form (inside DEFINE [ ]) omits it.
block_form.example_standalone: DEFINE NAMESPACE Core.Game [ DEFINE FIELD level: Int; ];
block_form.example_contained: DEFINE [ NAMESPACE Core.Game [ FIELD level: Int ] ];

normative_rules.name: Nesting & Hierarchy
normative_rules.description: Contained namespaces may nest arbitrarily. A sub-namespace declared in block form within another follows the dot-hierarchy. Dotted names (e.g. Core.Game.Combat) are valid for inline declarations.

normative_rules.name: Contained Scope Prefixes
normative_rules.description: Inside a DEFINE [ ] block, NAMESPACE contents omit the DEFINE keyword. Standalone block forms MUST include the DEFINE keyword for each entry.

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] ENUM EnumName<TYPE?> { ... } | DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] ENUM [ Enum1 { ... }, Enum2 { ... } ];
definitions.description: Defines named constants. Body is { }. Supports Level 2 batching via [ ].
definitions.example: DEFINE ENUM Priority<INT> { LOW = 1, MEDIUM = 2, HIGH = 3 };
definitions.batch_syntax: DEFINE ENUM [ Status { ACTIVE, INACTIVE }, Role { ADMIN, USER } ];

variants.INT: Integer-backed. Enables range queries. All constants must have explicit = value.
variants.DECIMAL: Fixed-point decimal (requires 'd' suffix). Exact equality safe. Range enabled.
variants.STRING: Explicit string values for external interop/serialization.
variants.FLAGS: Bitfield (max 64 constants). Enables set operations (|, &, ~, IN). Backing uN type optimized automatically.

rules: Backing values are identity markers, NOT arithmetic operands. Use case-extraction or primitive fields for math.
Duplicate values within an enum are forbidden [2061].
FLAGS constants must not have manual assignments [2062].

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] FIELD FieldName: DataType? [@decorator] [DEFAULT expression];
definitions.description: Mandatory global property definition. Every property used in a type body must be declared here first.

new_structural_constraint_decorators.description: Enforces a lower bound (inclusive) at write time.
Enforces an upper bound (inclusive) at write time.
Enforces minimum character length at write time.
Enforces maximum character length at write time.
Enforces a regular expression match at write time.
Documents and enforces the precision and scale of the field.

notes: Fields are non-null by default. Append `?` to type for nullable fields.
Node<T> fields store a reference to another node by its _id. Use Node<T>? for optional references.
Decorators (@unique, @index, @required, @readonly, @min, @max, @minlength, @maxlength, @pattern, @precision) are structural metadata.
@index on a Node<T> field creates a reverse index, enabling fast lookups for parent nodes referencing a specific child.

Decorator vs Constraint Rule: If a validation is universally true for this field in every node, edge, or trait that will ever use it — it is a decorator on DEFINE FIELD. If a validation is specific to a type, references multiple fields, or encodes a business rule — it is a named constraint on the type. Structural constraint decorators (@min, @max, etc.) are evaluated at write-time and apply only to non-null values.
Mandatory: Every field in a NODE, EDGE, STRUCT, or TRAIT must have a matching DEFINE FIELD.

default_expr_union.description: DEFAULT values are formally typed as a DefaultExpr union. Each variant has distinct validation rules applied at definition time.

variants.name: LiteralDefault
variants.validation: Type must match field type exactly. Validated at definition time.

variants.name: NowDefault
variants.validation: Valid only on Date and DateTime fields. Always permitted regardless of other field decorators.

variants.name: UuidDefault
variants.validation: Valid only on UUID fields. Always permitted.

variants.name: PureUdfDefault
variants.validation: Called function must be declared @pure. @readonly and @nondeterministic UDFs are forbidden as defaults. Validated at definition time via purity check.

variants.name: EnumVariantDefault
variants.validation: Must be a valid variant of the field's declared enum type. Validated at definition time.

definitions.default_resolution_order: 1. Explicit value in CREATE > 2. Node/Edge override > 3. Global Field default > 4. null (if nullable) > 5. Error [3015]

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] FUNCTION @purity Name(params): ReturnType { body };
definitions.description: Defines a scripted User-Defined Function (UDF). Requires a mandatory purity decorator (@pure, @readonly, @nondeterministic).
definitions.example: DEFINE FUNCTION @pure FullName(first: String, last: String): String { RETURN first + " " + last; };
notes: Purity is statically validated at definition time.
Call-graph transitivity applies (e.g., @pure cannot call @readonly).
UDFs are interpreted; performance warnings apply in high-volume queries.
v0.19: Function body must have at least one reachable RETURN path [1051].

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] AGGREGATE FUNCTION @pure FunctionName(params): ReturnType { STATE [ slot_name: SlotType = initial_expr, ... ]; ACCUMULATE [ slot_name = accumulate_expr, ... ]; FINALIZE finalize_expr; };
definitions.description: Defines a User-Defined Aggregate Function (UDAF). Mandatory structure includes STATE, ACCUMULATE, and FINALIZE clauses.
definitions.example: DEFINE AGGREGATE FUNCTION @pure WeightedAvg(val: Float, weight: Float): Float { STATE [ total_weighted: Float = 0.0, total_weight: Float = 0.0 ]; ACCUMULATE [ total_weighted = total_weighted + (val * weight), total_weight = total_weight + weight ]; FINALIZE IF total_weight == 0.0 THEN 0.0 ELSE total_weighted / total_weight; };

clauses.STATE: Declares the accumulator. Each slot has a name, type, and mandatory initial value (literals or @pure calls only). Must be primitive or Struct<T>.
clauses.ACCUMULATE: Evaluated once per input row. Every slot must be assigned exactly once. Parameters and current slot values are in scope.
clauses.FINALIZE: Evaluated once after processing. Only STATE slots are in scope. Parameters are NOT in scope.

scope_rules.ACCUMULATE: Input parameters, STATE slot names (current values)

notes: Must be marked @pure [2056].
FINALIZE is always called exactly once, even for empty input sets (using initial STATE).
Graph-referencing types are forbidden in STATE slots.

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] STRUCT StructName { FieldRef, ... }
definitions.description: A Struct is a value object. It has no identity, cannot be connected to edges, cannot be queried directly, and exists only embedded within Nodes or other Structs. Fields are stored physically inline within the containing node's column store with no pointer indirection. Structs are globally defined. A Struct<Address> used across Person, Company, and Location resolves to the same definition everywhere, ensuring consistent physical layout across all containing types. Structs are NOT Nodes or Traits. Nodes carry identity via _id; Node<T> fields store references to those identities. Structs are pure value containers with guaranteed storage locality. They serve different functions and should not be merged.

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] TRAIT TraitName [EXTENDS [Trait1, Trait2]] { FieldRef, ... } [MetadataBlock]
definitions.description: Traits are the abstraction mechanism. They are never instantiated but are queryable via polymorphic MATCH, participate in role ALLOWS resolution, and carry inheritable named constraints. Field composition is via global DEFINE FIELD references only [1052].
properties: Composable via EXTENDS from other Traits
Queryable via polymorphic MATCH — returns all concrete nodes that EXTEND this Trait
Valid in role ALLOWS clauses — all concrete subtypes automatically qualify
Can carry named constraints — inherited by all extending types
Field composition via global DEFINE FIELD references only [1052]
examples: DEFINE TRAIT Identifiable { id, created_at } { display: id };
DEFINE TRAIT Auditable { created_at, updated_at, created_by } { constraints: { valid_update_time: updated_at >= created_at } };
MATCH (e:Auditable) WHERE e.created_at > "2025-01-01" RETURN e, TYPE(e);
DEFINE EDGE Owns { owner <- (ONE) ALLOWS Identifiable, asset <- (ONE) ALLOWS Trackable };

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] NODE NodeTypeName [EXTENDS [Type1, Type2]] { Entry, ... } [MetadataBlock]
definitions.description: Defines a strict Node Type with optional entity-level metadata (display label and constraints). Supports multiple inheritance via EXTENDS and node-level DEFAULT overrides. v0.19: Requires bare field references (FieldRef) for storage fields [1052].

entry_types.FieldRef: Bare field name reference (must match a DEFINE FIELD). Supports primitive, Struct<T>, and Node<T> types.
entry_types.FieldRef DEFAULT expr: Field name reference with a type-local default override.
entry_types.ComputedFieldRef: Identifier : ReturnType @computed(...) - inline computed field declaration.

metadata_block.description: Optional block containing per-type metadata. Keys 'display' and 'constraints' are both optional and may appear in any order. Anonymous constraints are no longer supported.

display_label.description: User-declared canonical display label for the type. Resolved to a SchemaId at definition time. Inherited from a single unambiguous parent if not declared.

object_form.description: Named constraints for better error reporting and documentation. This is the only valid syntax for constraints.
object_form.example: constraints: { valid_age: age >= 0 AND age <= 150, has_name: name != "" }

constraint_name_scoping.scope: Constraint names are unique per type. All constraints must be user-declared.
constraint_name_scoping.drop_by_name: DROP CONSTRAINT is strictly name-only. Users must reference a user-declared name.
constraint_name_scoping.example: ALTER NODE Person DROP CONSTRAINT valid_age;

definitions.constraint_context: Can reference 'this' and all node fields, including @computed properties.
definitions.example: DEFINE NODE Person { id, name, age, status DEFAULT AccountStatus.PENDING } { display: name, constraints: { valid_age: age >= 0 AND age <= 150 } };
notes: Metadata block is optional. Omit if no display label or constraints are needed.
Node-level DEFAULT overrides global field defaults for that specific type.

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] ABSTRACT EDGE EdgeTypeName [EXTENDS [Type1, Type2]] { Entry, ... } [MetadataBlock]
definitions.description: Abstract edges enable polymorphic edge traversal. A query matching on an abstract edge type returns all concrete edge instances whose types EXTEND it. Retain only if polymorphic edge traversal is required by the schema. Concrete edges that happen to share fields should use Trait-based field composition via EXTENDS rather than abstract edge typing unless traversal polymorphism is specifically needed.
definitions.example: DEFINE ABSTRACT EDGE Transaction { initiator <- (ONE) ALLOWS [Person, Organization], transaction_date };

metadata_block.description: Optional block containing per-type metadata. Anonymous constraints are no longer supported.

constraint_name_scoping.scope: Constraint names are unique per type. All constraints must be user-declared.
constraint_name_scoping.drop_by_name: DROP CONSTRAINT is strictly name-only. Users must reference a user-declared name.

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] EDGE EdgeTypeName [EXTENDS [Type1, Type2]] { Entry, ... } [MetadataBlock]
definitions.description: Defines a strict Hyperedge with optional relationship-level metadata. Supports multiple inheritance and strictly typed localized Roles with extended cardinality.

entry_types.RoleRef: RoleName Direction (Cardinality) [ALLOWS AllowsClause] [ConstraintBlock] - localized role declaration.

metadata_block.description: Optional block containing per-type metadata. Anonymous constraints are no longer supported.

definitions.cardinality: Extended cardinality supports exact (N), unbounded (*), and range (N..M) counts. Legacy ONE (1) and MANY (*) remain as aliases.

object_form.description: Named constraints for better error reporting and documentation.
object_form.example: constraints: { different_people: husband != wife, valid_date: date <= NOW() }

constraint_name_scoping.scope: Constraint names are unique per type. All constraints must be user-declared.
constraint_name_scoping.drop_by_name: DROP CONSTRAINT is strictly name-only. Users must reference a user-declared name.

definitions.constraint_context: Can reference all role variables and edge fields, including @computed properties.
definitions.example: DEFINE EDGE Marriage { husband <- (1) ALLOWS Person, wife <- (1) ALLOWS Person, date DEFAULT NOW() } { display: date, constraints: { different_people: husband != wife, valid_date: date <= NOW() } };
notes: Optional Roles: Use (0..1) cardinality. Legacy '?' suffix is deprecated [WARN-SCHEMA-002].
Cardinality Enforcement: Bounds are enforced on CREATE and all SET += / -= mutations [3014].
Directionality: <- indicates Source, -> indicates Target, <-> indicates Bidirectional (Symmetric).
Bidirectional Roles (<->): Semantically symmetric. Traversal matches both directed (->, <-) and undirected (-) patterns. Role access (edge.role) returns all bound nodes.
Edge Field Defaults: DEFAULT on edge fields overrides global field defaults.

Edge Inheritance: When an edge EXTENDS another, it inherits all roles from the parent. Inherited roles may be overridden by redeclaring them with the same name (which fully replaces parent constraints), or supplemented by adding new roles.
Validation: Requires two+ distinct roles OR one role with cardinality > 1.

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [ ENUM [...], FIELD [...], STRUCT [...], TRAIT [...], NODE [...], EDGE [...], VIEW [...], UNION [...], INDEX [...] ];
definitions.description: Anonymous mixed definition block. Hoisting applies across the entire block; definition order does not affect validity.
definitions.example: DEFINE [ FIELD [ id: UUID ], NODE [ Person { id } ] ];

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] VIEW ViewName AS QueryBody; | DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] VIEW ViewName ($param: Type, ...) AS QueryBody;
definitions.description: Defines a named, reusable query fragment that expands inline at planning time. No dedicated storage partition is created. Results are always current. Named views are composable — a view may reference other named views.
examples: DEFINE VIEW ActiveUsers AS MATCH (u:User) WHERE u.status == .ACTIVE AND u.last_login > DATE_ADD(NOW(), -30, DAY) RETURN u;
DEFINE VIEW RecentActivity ($days: Int) AS MATCH (u:User) WHERE u.last_login > DATE_ADD(NOW(), -$days, DAY) RETURN u;
definitions.usage: MATCH (u) FROM ActiveUsers WHERE u.department == "Engineering" RETURN u;
properties: Expanded inline at query planning time
EXPLAIN shows the full expanded plan, not the view name
Subject to synchronous revalidation on schema ALTER
Parameters use the same $param syntax as prepared statements
Can reference other named views (no circular references)
Cannot reference MATERIALIZED VIEW results directly
No REBUILD operation — always current by definition

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] UNION UnionName { VariantName { FieldRef, ... }, ... };
definitions.description: Defines a tagged union type for use as a UDF return type. Each variant is a named value container with its own fields. Union types may only be used as UDF return type annotations. They are not node types, cannot be stored, and cannot be queried.
definitions.example: DEFINE UNION SearchResult { Hit { score: Float, node_id: UUID }, Miss { reason: String }, Error { code: Int, message: String } };
rules: Variant names must be unique within the union
Fields within variants follow global DEFINE FIELD rules [1052]
Union types cannot EXTEND other types
Union types cannot appear in DEFINE NODE, DEFINE EDGE, DEFINE TRAIT, or DEFINE STRUCT bodies
Exhaustive pattern matching is required in MATCH expressions over a union type

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] SCHEMA SchemaName [ ...batch definitions... ];
definitions.description: Creates a named, versionable, and importable schema unit. Preferred for modular architectures.
definitions.example: DEFINE SCHEMA Family [ FIELD [ ... ], NODE [ ... ], EDGE [ ... ] ];

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] MATERIALIZED VIEW ViewName FOR [Types] ON [Fields] INDEX [Fields];
definitions.description: Creates a pre-computed cross-type index partition to optimize CROSS_TYPE queries.
definitions.example: DEFINE MATERIALIZED VIEW PersonSearch FOR [Person, Employee] ON [LastName] INDEX [LastName];

definitions.syntax: DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] INDEX IndexName ON NodeType (Field1, Field2, ...); | DEFINE [IF NOT EXISTS] INDEX [ ... ];
definitions.description: Creates a composite index on multiple fields for optimized multi-field queries. Supports batch syntax.
definitions.batch_syntax: DEFINE INDEX [ Index1 ON Type1 (F1), Index2 ON Type2 (F2, F3) ];
definitions.example: DEFINE INDEX NameIndex ON Person (LastName, FirstName);

migration.syntax: ALTER NODE TypeName AlterOp | ALTER NODE TypeName [ AlterOp, ... ] | ALTER NODE [ TypeName [ AlterOp, ... ], ... ] | ALTER [ NODE [ ... ], EDGE [ ... ] ] | ALTER FIELD FieldName AlterFieldOp
migration.description: Modifies existing definitions (NODE, EDGE, FIELD). Follows the 4-level hierarchy and uses [ ] for batches of operations or types.
alter_rules: ADD CONSTRAINT: All constraints must be named (Name: Expr). Anonymous constraints are no longer supported.
DROP CONSTRAINT: Strictly name-based. No expression matching supported.
EDGE ROLE: Supports sub-level role operations: DROP ROLE spouse, ADD ROLE husband <- (1) ALLOWS Person, ADD ROLE [ r1 <- (1) ALLOWS T1, r2 <- (*) ALLOWS T2 ].
ALTER FIELD: Supports SET TYPE, ADD/DROP @decorator, SET/DROP DEFAULT. Changing type or adding @unique requires data revalidation.
v0.20: Triggers synchronous revalidation of stored QueryPlans. All existing data must satisfy new constraints or ALTER fails [3030].

migration.syntax: ALTER SCHEMA SchemaName [ ADD FieldRef | NodeRef | EdgeRef, DROP FieldRef | NodeRef | EdgeRef, RENAME OldName TO NewName ];
migration.description: Modifies a schema unit. Triggers synchronous QueryPlan revalidation for all plans referencing any type within the schema. Dropping a construct referenced elsewhere fails with [3031].
migration.example: ALTER SCHEMA Family [ ADD NODE Employee EXTENDS Person { employee_id, hire_date } ];

migration.description: Non-destructive. Validates all constraints, field references, and inter-type consistency within the schema against existing data. Returns SchemaValidationResult.
Non-destructive preview of migration. Checks field mapping, default application, and edge cascade compatibility. Edge cascade rule: target type must be ALLOWED by all existing connected roles.

migration.syntax: MIGRATE variable TO NewType [MAP { old_field: new_field, DROP [field1, field2] }] [DEFAULTS { field: value }]
migration.description: Type conversion operation. Destructive by design. Evaluates edge cascade compatibility: all connected edges must satisfy role ALLOWS lists and role constraints for the target type. Fails with [3012] if any edge violation occurs.

decorators.name: @computed
decorators.description: Defines a virtual property calculated at Read-Time using the Standard Expression Language. v0.19 internal representation uses ComputedSpec union: Expression(scalar expr) or Traverse(QueryPlan).

decorators.name: @computed(TRAVERSE)
decorators.description: Defines a virtual property calculated via graph traversal query.
decorators.evaluation_model: Per-Row Memoization within a QueryPlan context. Subquery executes once per node on first access within a query. Cached for the duration of that query execution.
decorators.details: For production schemas where read performance is critical, use @materialized to move cost to write time. For cases where memoization is undesirable, unmaterialized @computed(TRAVERSE) re-executes per query but still memoizes within a single query execution.

performance_warning.issue: Using in WHERE clauses forces N executions. Production schemas should use @materialized. [WARN-PERF-001]

decorators.name: @pure
decorators.description: Mandatory decorator for UDFs. Logic and arithmetic only. No graph access or non-determinism. Safe for constraints and DEFAULT expressions.

decorators.name: @readonly
decorators.description: Mandatory decorator for UDFs. May perform graph traversal (MATCH). Deterministic. Safe for computed(TRAVERSE) and queries. Forbidden in DEFAULT expressions.

decorators.name: @nondeterministic
decorators.description: Mandatory decorator for UDFs. May use non-deterministic built-ins like NOW() or UUID(). Not safe for constraints or memoized caching. Safe for DEFAULT expressions.

decorators.name: @deferred
decorators.description: Defers constraint validation until transaction commit. @deferred requires a named constraint. Forbidden on role ALLOWS constraint blocks [1060]. Evaluation failure at commit rolls back the transaction.
decorators.placement: May be applied to an individual named constraint entry or to an entire named constraint block.
decorators.example: constraints: { mutual_spouse: husband.spouse == wife @deferred, valid_date: date <= NOW() }

decorators.name: @materialized
decorators.description: Pre-computes and caches results of @computed(TRAVERSE) properties, moving cost from read-time to write-time. STRONGLY PREFERRED for production schemas. v0.19: Recomputed on write triggers derived from the QueryPlan. Forbidden on @computed(EXPRESSION) fields [2072].
decorators.update_trigger: Recomputed on write operations affecting the traversal pattern

performance_notes.read_cost: O(1) lookup, same as regular property access
performance_notes.storage_cost: Cached value stored per node in primary column store
performance_notes.recommendation: Use for frequently-read aggregations; schema design signal for WHERE clause performance.

decorators.name: @unique
decorators.description: Enforces global uniqueness. Can be applied to fields or Edge Roles (composite uniqueness). v0.19: Edge constraints represented via UniqueConstraintMember (role/field).
decorators.notes: Required for Role-Based MERGE on hyperedges. Composite uniqueness indexes can mix bound node IDs (roles) and field values (fields) in a single declaration.

decorators.name: @ordered
decorators.description: For (MANY) cardinality roles. Preserves insertion order. Stores as dynamic array.

decorators.name: @unordered
decorators.description: For (MANY) cardinality roles. Set semantics. Stores as open-addressing hash set.

index_types.name: @index
index_types.description: Creates an index for fast lookups. Default is B-Tree index.

types.use_case: Similarity search for embeddings. Requires SIMD alignment.

decorators.purpose: Structural metadata, indexing, and storage hints
decorators.evaluation: Enforced by storage layer and type system
decorators.scope: Single field, function, or structural property

constraints.scope: Cross-field validation, entity invariants, relationship rules

decorator_vs_constraint_distinction.key_difference: @unique is a structural guarantee (creates index), not a business rule. Constraints express domain logic.

composition_vs_association.rule: Use Node<T> for composition (identity-based containment). Use Edges/Roles for association (bidirectional relationships, reverse traversal).
composition_vs_association.example: A Team should use a Node<Person> field for its 'lead' (composition). A Person should use an 'IsMemberOf' edge to associate with a Team (association), enabling bidirectional traversal.

complex.name: Enum<Name>
complex.desc: Restricted value set. Supports typed variants (INT, DECIMAL, STRING). v0.19 resolution pass converts shorthands.

complex.name: Flags<Name>
complex.desc: Bitfield of combinable constants. Enables |, &, ~, IN operators.

complex.name: Node<T>
complex.desc: Reference to a node of type T by its _id. Identity-based composition.

complex.name: List<Node<T>>
complex.desc: Collection of references to nodes of type T. Supports @ordered/@unordered decorators and atomicity.

cardinality.name: Unbounded
cardinality.desc: 1 or more target nodes (Legacy MANY alias).

cardinality.name: Range
cardinality.desc: Between N and M nodes. N >= 0. M can be * for unbounded.

cardinality.name: Optional
cardinality.desc: Zero or one target node. Replaces legacy '?' suffix.

special.name: PATH
special.desc: Result type from variable-length path queries. v0.19: Formally represented as a Path struct containing a sequence of PathSegments.

fields.name: node
fields.note: The node at this position in the path.

fields.name: via_edge
fields.note: The edge used to arrive at this node. null for the first segment (path origin).

fields.name: via_role
fields.note: The SchemaId of the role traversed on via_edge. null for the first segment.

fields.name: segments
fields.desc: The full ordered sequence of segments.

fields.name: total_cost
fields.desc: Total accumulated weight. 0.0 for unweighted paths.

fields.name: length
fields.desc: Number of edges traversed (segment count minus one).

field_accessors.path.nodes: []NodeId — shorthand for all node values across segments
field_accessors.path.edges: []EdgeId — shorthand for all non-null via_edge values
field_accessors.path.length: u32 — number of edges in the path
field_accessors.path.start: NodeId — first node in the path
field_accessors.path.end: NodeId — last node in the path

special.predicate_semantics: ALL/ANY/NONE accept path.nodes (binds NodeId), path.edges (binds EdgeId), or path.segments (binds PathSegment) as the iteration target.
special.materialized_note: When @materialized, the cached value is the serialized Path struct. Cleared on next write trigger if any referenced IDs are deleted. Null if no path currently exists.

warnings.WARN-SCHEMA-002: Deprecated ? role suffix — use (0..1) cardinality instead
warnings.WARN-SCHEMA-003: Inline Field Declaration (Pre-v0.19) — v0.19 requires extraction to DEFINE FIELD.
warnings.WARN-PERF-001: Traversal-computed property used in WHERE clause without @materialized
warnings.WARN-PERF-004: Dynamic Traversal Materialization: Emitted when a CROSS_TYPE query falls back to a scan because of stale/missing views, or when a @computed(TRAVERSE) @materialized field has incomplete write-trigger derivation.
